title: fix(app-shell): a keyboard drag in the form designer reaches a drop target (objectui#11871)
body:
Fixes #11871

Clause-②: no

## What changes

The Studio form designer's `DndContext` now gets its collision detection from a module-private `formCollision` in `ObjectFormDesigner.tsx`:

- a pointer drag (pointer coordinates present): `pointerWithin`, exactly as before;
- a keyboard drag (no pointer coordinates): `closestCorners`.

Before, `pointerWithin` answered no droppable for every keyboard drag, because dnd-kit reads pointer coordinates off the activator event and a `KeyboardEvent` has none. `over` stayed empty, `onDragEnd` returned without committing, and the live region said the field was dropped outside the groups.

Why `closestCorners` and not `closestCenter`: both committed every keyboard move in the browser reading below, with the same sentences. `closestCorners` is the measure `sortableKeyboardCoordinates` (the keyboard sensor's coordinate getter) picks each arrow-key step's target by, so the drag is over the droppable the step moved it to. A section droppable also contains its field droppables, the nested case where a one-field section's centre can coincide with its field's centre.

Handlers: `onDragOver` and `onDragEnd` are unchanged. A keyboard drop reaches the same commit as a pointer drop through the existing arithmetic, measured below. `formDndAnnouncements.ts`, `SortableField`, `isKeptOffLayout`, the sensors and their wiring, every `package.json`, `packages/components/src/ui/**` and `packages/i18n/**` are untouched. No export, prop or accepted input changes.

## Mechanism readings (the dispatch's H1 to H3)

- **H1 holds.** In source, `pointerWithin` returns an empty list when `pointerCoordinates` is null, and `getEventCoordinates` returns null for an event without `clientX`, which a `KeyboardEvent` is. In real Chromium on `origin/main` `3035948`, seven keyboard sequences (within a group, into another group, into the empty group, the card's own steps) made zero commits, each ending "... was dropped outside the groups and is back in ...". The three pointer drags each committed.
- **H2 holds for a one-column canvas, and is partly falsified for a multi-column one.** One column (480px viewport): each arrow-key step lands `over` on the next field card (`f:`), or on the section droppable (`g:`) of an empty group. Multi-column (1280px viewport, two or three fields per row): the getter steps card to card and never targets a section droppable, because its corner distance to a full-width section loses to the nearest card.
- **H3 holds for one column, and is falsified for multi-column.** One column: ArrowDown from Email lands `over` `g:new_group`; `onDragOver` moves Email into the group; `over` then becomes Email's own card, and `onDragEnd`'s same-container branch commits that place unchanged. That is the same two-step the pointer path makes (objectui#11802's browser reading). Multi-column: the arrow keys never reach the empty group. ArrowDown from Email lands in Ungrouped, position 2 of 3, and ArrowUp from Name lands in Contact, position 1 of 3. That is the keyboard coordinate getter, outside this card's fence, so it is reported as a finding and not changed here.

## Browser reading (real Chromium, dev-only harness, never committed)

A dev-only Vite page mounted the same `ObjectFormDesigner` the Form tab mounts (`readOnly` off, sensors on) with objectui#11802's fixture: Contact (Phone, Email), New group (empty), Ungrouped (Name, Industry). Playwright drove it with keyboard presses on the committed source (`7455f4e`; the merge with `main` does not touch `ObjectFormDesigner.tsx`).

| Keys | Viewport | Live region at the drop | Committed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phone: Space, ArrowDown, Space | 480 | Phone moved to Contact, position 2 of 2. | Contact: email, phone |
| Phone: Space, ArrowRight, Space | 1280 | Phone moved to Contact, position 2 of 2. | Contact: email, phone |
| Email: Space, ArrowDown, Space | 480 | Email moved to New group, position 1 of 1. | New group: email |
| Email: Space, ArrowDown, Space | 1280 | Email moved to Ungrouped, position 2 of 3. | Ungrouped: name, email, industry |
| Name: Space, ArrowUp three times, Space | 480 | Name moved to Contact, position 2 of 3. | Contact: phone, name, email |
| F6: Space, ArrowUp, Space (11 fields, 3 per row) | 1280 | F6 moved to Contact, position 4 of 7. | Contact: f1, f2, f3, f6, f4, f5, notes |
| Industry: Space, ArrowDown three times, Space (the card's steps) | both | Industry moved to Ungrouped, position 2 of 2. | order unchanged (Industry is the last field) |

Pointer control, same harness after the change: Name onto New group gives "Name moved to New group, position 1 of 1."; Phone onto Email commits Contact: email, phone; Name onto Email commits Contact: phone, name, email. These are the same sentences and commits as on `origin/main`.

## Tests

New: `ObjectFormDesigner.keyboardDrop-11871.test.tsx`. It runs the real `DndContext`, `KeyboardSensor` with `sortableKeyboardCoordinates`, `PointerSensor`, and the designer's collision detection and handlers; nothing in `@dnd-kit` is mocked. The test DOM does no layout, so a `getBoundingClientRect` stub lays the canvas out from the one-column Chromium reading above, including the drag overlay's label chip, which dnd-kit measures as the dragged box. Five keyboard cases assert what Chromium did with the same keys (the live region and the committed `fields`). Two pointer cases are the control.

Reverse checks, one-off, through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (mutation proven on disk; restore proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`):

- `formCollision` reverted to `pointerWithin` alone: 5 failed, 2 passed. Every keyboard case went red in the predicted direction, with no commit: "Industry was dropped outside the groups and is back in Ungrouped, position 2 of 2." and "Email was dropped outside the groups and is back in Contact, position 2 of 2.". The two pointer cases stayed green.
- `closestCorners` on every drag, pointer included: 1 failed, 6 passed. The pointer control "a pointer released outside every group commits nothing" went red ("Name moved to New group, position 1 of 1."). A first attempt, whose replacement text already occurred inside the anchor, was refused by the tool as a no-op and restored; the run above is the second.

## Acceptance notes

- **The card's own steps.** Industry is the last field on the canvas, so ArrowDown has nowhere to take it, before or after this change. What changes for those steps is the drop: it lands on Industry's own place and says so, instead of "dropped outside the groups".
- **A pick-up and drop in place commits the unchanged layout,** through `onDragEnd`'s existing `commit(prev)` for a drop on the field's own card. A pointer drag released on its own card does the same; the keyboard now reaches that commit too.
- **Measured and not changed here** (the keyboard coordinate getter and the shared drop arithmetic, outside this card's fence; reported to the seat): in a multi-column canvas the arrow keys never reach an empty group, and a full-width card (`textarea`) cannot step up; the first ArrowUp from a group's first field moves nothing, because the getter's first target is the field's own section; entering a group that has fields from above, the over sentence says position 1 and the drop lands at position 2, the same `onDragEnd` arithmetic objectui#11802 pins for a pointer drop still over the field it was carried onto.

Changeset: `.changeset/11871-form-designer-keyboard-drop.md`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.
